transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Sunridge - Dir InfoSec), Elena Ruiz (Sunridge - Procurement), Tommy Chen (Sunridge - Eng)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll get started. i'm jordan from redwood, i run the account, with priya here who is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya Nambiar: hi all, priya, i'll walk through the security sections of the SIG and answer tech questions, and we'll flag where you need evidence.
[00:20] Marcus Hale: great, thanks. to be clear we're primarily concerned about SOC 2 controls, data residency for regulated workloads, RBAC and SSO integration, and how keys are managed for encryption.
[00:33] Elena Ruiz: and procurement will need the completed SIG and SOC report for vendor review.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: perfect, that's what we planned. quick agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, identity and access (RBAC, SSO, SCIM), audit logs retention and exports, encryption/KMS and BYOK, data residency and certs, then open Q&A and next steps.
[00:52] Priya Nambiar: jumping into section 1, SOC 2 we are SOC 2 Type II, our report covers the past 12 months. we can provide a redacted report and we also have penetration test summaries and our vulnerability management process doc.
[01:05] Marcus Hale: can you share the last penetration test results and remediation timeline? infosec wants to verify critical findings were resolved.
[01:11] Priya Nambiar: yes, we'll share the exec summary and remediation evidence. note sometimes vendor reports redact customer identifiers, we'll provide timestamps for patching windows.
[01:22] Jordan Lee: action: i'll upload SOC2 and pentest summary to the shared folder after the call.
[01:28] Marcus Hale: ok thanks. next, section on identity — how does SSO work? we use Okta and need SAML S S O and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:36] Priya Nambiar: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning. we also support Just-in-Time provisioning if you don't want SCIM, but SCIM is the recommended approach for enterprise. we'll provide SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint details.
[01:52] Tommy Chen: how are roles mapped? we need RBAC that aligns to our internal roles (viewer/operator/admin).
[01:58] Priya Nambiar: roles are configurable. we have built-in roles and you can map SAML attributes or use SCIM groups. we log role assignment changes and have an admin audit trail.
[02:10] Marcus Hale: retention on those audit logs? regulators require 1 year minimum, sometimes 3.
[02:16] Priya Nambiar: default is 12 months in the console, and we can provide longer retention as an add-on. we can also stream logs to your SIEM via S3 export or syslog connector — many banks connect to Splunk/Datadog via our S3 delivery.
[02:35] Elena Ruiz: when you say S3 export, is that encrypted? who owns the keys?
[02:40] Priya Nambiar: good question — exports are encrypted in transit and at rest. you can configure a customer-managed KMS key (BYOK) for S3 exports and for primary data encryption as well.
[02:51] Jordan Lee: to be explicit: we offer both service-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. for customers with strict controls you can request BYOK and we support HSM-based key wrapping.
[03:05] Marcus Hale: do you support hardware security modules for key escrow? internal policy needs HSM-backed KMS for production keys.
[03:11] Priya Nambiar: yes, we support HSM-backed KMS through the cloud provider's KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with CloudHSM) or via a bring-your-own-HSM approach for private deployments. we'll cover options in the technical deep dive.
[03:26] Tommy Chen: are encryption keys rotated automatically and what's the rotation policy?
[03:30] Priya Nambiar: rotation can be automated; default is 90 days but you can set custom rotation windows and we store rotation history.
[03:37] Jordan Lee: moving to data residency — you mentioned regulated data needs to stay in US east.
[03:42] Marcus Hale: yes, production PII must remain in us-east or on-prem in our VPC.
[03:46] Priya Nambiar: in hosted we can pin request routing to a region and we have dedicated region deployments in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and gce variants. for stricter needs we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) which gives you full network control.
[04:02] Marcus Hale: for the SIG answers, we'll need clear evidence of region isolation and data flow diagrams.
[04:08] Priya Nambiar: we'll include architecture diagrams and our data flow document. note that some logs (control-plane telemetry) may traverse our control plane for observability; we can provide details and redaction options.
[04:22] Elena Ruiz: procurement asks about third-party sub processors and vendor list.
[04:27] Jordan Lee: we'll attach our current subprocessor list and a link to the privacy policy and DPA.
[04:33] Marcus Hale: ok thanks. next: auditability and evidence in SIG for control OV-3 etc. for the SIG there's often requests for policy docs, org charts, and access review cadence.
[04:44] Priya Nambiar: we have templates: org chart, written security policies (incident response, RBAC), annual access review process, tabletop exercise reports. we'll zip these for evidence.
[04:56] Tommy Chen: on the technical side, do you provide immutable audit logs or are they editable by admins?
[05:02] Priya Nambiar: audit logs are immutable, stored with append-only semantics; only export and read access is available. administrative actions are also logged and we provide signed log timestamps for critical events.
[05:15] Marcus Hale: any SOC 2 exceptions or scope exclusions we should be aware of?
[05:20] Jordan Lee: the SOC 2 cover letter will list scope; we've excluded some internal dev-only labs, but production inference and data plane are in scope. we'll flag that in the uploaded report.
[05:35] Elena Ruiz: procurement wants to know about liability caps and standard contract terms.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: i can have legal provide our standard terms and we can discuss specific adjustments as needed — that usually goes through our legal channel after vendor acceptance.
[05:49] Marcus Hale: ok. moving to SIG question 3.4 on encryption at rest, can you point to where we document key management?
[05:56] Priya Nambiar: yes section 3.4 answer will reference our KMS page and we'll attach a diagram showing key lifecycle and rotation logs.
[06:10] Tommy Chen: how about network isolation — can we run in a single-tenant VPC?
[06:15] Priya Nambiar: Redwood Dedicated offers dedicated GPU pools in a single-tenant environment with configurable VPC peering and private endpoints. Private deployments give full on-prem control.
[06:27] Marcus Hale: any experience integrating with our internal PAM? we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets.
[06:33] Priya Nambiar: we have integrations and an API for secrets retrieval. for BYOK we can wrap keys with Vault or plug into KMS via our connector; we'll show patterns in the deep dive.
[06:45] Jordan Lee: competitor question — how do we differentiate from BigCloudAI?
[06:49] Priya Nambiar: our main difference is production-grade serving with observable rollouts, and flexible private deployment options; we provide more transparent unit economics and built-in evasion/fallbacks.
[06:59] Marcus Hale: noted.
[07:02] Elena Ruiz: procurement question on evidence delivery — can you put everything in a secure folder?
[07:07] Jordan Lee: yes we'll provision a secure share (S3 presigned links / secure share) and control access. we'll send the link via the CRM ticket.
[07:17] Marcus Hale: one more on incident response — RTO/RPO and notification windows?
[07:22] Priya Nambiar: we maintain IR runbooks, 24/7 on-call, and we have a SLA for incident notification: critical incidents notified within 1 hour and postmortem within 72 hours for severity 1. RTO/RPO depend on deployment and can be contractual for Dedicated/Private.
[07:40] Tommy Chen: do you provide evidence of tabletop exercises?
[07:44] Priya Nambiar: yes we can share summaries and outcomes for recent tabletop exercises, redacted where necessary.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: let's talk about the SIG itself — there are about 200 questions, we'll pre-fill the easy ones and highlight items needing evidence. the typical flow is we send a draft SIG, you review, then we hand over evidence links.
[08:06] Marcus Hale: timeline — procurement wants the vendor pack by end of month. is that feasible?
[08:12] Jordan Lee: yes if we get the go-ahead we'll aim to deliver the draft SIG and SOC2 by 2026-05-22.
[08:20] Elena Ruiz: what about penetration test evidence format? pdf with executive summary and remediation tickets?
[08:25] Priya Nambiar: yes, we provide a pdf exec summary and a remediation table; we can also provide JIRA ticket references if needed by auditors.
[08:34] Marcus Hale: on legal/minimums, would you accept our standard security addendum?
[08:39] Jordan Lee: we can review it; legal typically reviews and we can negotiate specific clauses.
[08:44] Tommy Chen: for the technical deep dive — who should be on that call from your side?
[08:49] Priya Nambiar: i'll lead the deep dive with one of our infra engineers and a solution architect to cover KMS/BYOK and network topology.
[08:58] Marcus Hale: good.
[09:00] [longer segment skipped in recording — fast-forward noted]
[35:12] Priya Nambiar: picking back up on KMS: our BYOK flow supports key import and envelope encryption. customers can rotate keys on their schedule. evidence we can provide includes KMS audit logs, key creation timestamps, and HSM certification references.
[35:28] Marcus Hale: will the key material ever be exported by Redwood?
[35:32] Priya Nambiar: no, with BYOK the primary key material remains under customer control — we use key wrapping and never export customer private key material.
[35:40] Tommy Chen: what's the mechanism for log streaming to our SIEM?
[35:45] Priya Nambiar: we support S3 delivery encrypted with your KMS or a syslog endpoint; we also have a Kafka connector for high-volume customers.
[35:54] Marcus Hale: is there a compliance pack for auditors?
[35:58] Jordan Lee: we have a compliance bundle: SOC2 report, ISO certs if available, pen test exec summary, and a list of policies and org charts. we'll attach that bundle.
[36:08] Elena Ruiz: please ensure sensitive fields are redacted, procurement will not accept raw PII.
[36:12] Priya Nambiar: of course, all artifacts are redacted or redaction-ready.
[36:20] Jordan Lee: any open technical questions?
[36:23] Tommy Chen: one more: latency impact when using KMS for per-tenant encryption — any perf hit?
[36:29] Priya Nambiar: there is small crypto overhead for envelope unwrap on init, but runtime tokenization and KV cache reduce per-token KMS calls; we also support local key caches for performance with strict audit trails.
[36:46] Marcus Hale: ok that addresses it.
[36:50] Jordan Lee: let's recap next steps: we'll push SOC2 type II, pentest summary, subprocessor list, and a draft SIG with prefilled answers by 5/22. priya will share SAML metadata and SCIM guide by 5/25. tommy will share IP ranges and workload profile by 5/27. schedule deep dive week of 6/1.
[37:12] Elena Ruiz: sounds good. procurement will review once we have the draft SIG.
[37:17] Marcus Hale: thanks. any follow up items on legal?
[37:20] Jordan Lee: i'll loop in legal after the SOC2 upload, and we'll confirm contract points via CRM.
[37:27] Priya Nambiar: if you have specific SIG questions marked as 'requires evidence' we'll prioritize those docs.
[37:34] Marcus Hale: ok, thanks everyone.
[37:37] Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll send the share link and next steps via email and the CRM ticket. end call.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors noted in original: 'K M S' instead of KMS, 'S S O' spaced in places, speaker labels mixed briefly, some timestamps approximate.

References / Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-report (placeholder), https://redwood.example.com/docs/sso-scim-guide, shared folder link (to be provisioned).

End of transcript.
